findings.title: Retry cleanup is not restricted to SMS reminders
findings.body: The new `retryCount > 1` branch is a top-level OR condition with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` restriction. Consequently, any EMAIL or WHATSAPP `WorkflowReminder` whose retryCount is greater than one will be permanently deleted by this SMS cron endpoint, even though this retry policy is intended only for SMS. Scope the retry-count predicate to SMS reminders (and, if appropriate, unscheduled reminders) so this job cannot remove reminders owned by other delivery paths.

findings.title: Reminders with no renderable message or recipient never consume retries
findings.body: `retryCount` is only incremented after `scheduleSMS` returns false or throws. If `sendTo` is absent (possible because both the booking SMS number and workflow step recipient are optional) or message generation results in an empty value, this condition is skipped entirely. The reminder remains `scheduled: false` and is fetched on every cron run until its date passes, which leaves a common unsendable-SMS case unfixed by the retry cap. Treat an unusable recipient/message as a failed scheduling attempt, or delete/mark the reminder as unsendable.

findings.title: Retry count updates can lose increments when cron invocations overlap
findings.body: The handler reads `reminder.retryCount` and writes `reminder.retryCount + 1` rather than using an atomic database increment. Two overlapping cron requests can both read 0, both fail scheduling, and both write 1; the reminder then survives another run despite two failed attempts. Overlapping invocations are also especially plausible while a reminder remains unscheduled. Use Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }` update (and consider claiming the reminder/conditional updates to avoid concurrent scheduling) so the deletion threshold reflects actual failures.
